藏品名称_EN: East green glaze apricot round vase
描述_EN: An apricot-glazed round vase，the Qing dynasty (1840-1861)，your (honorific)30centimetre，bordering the mouth11.5centimetre，footrim13.2centimetre。　　Bottle with a rectangular body，straight edge of the mouth，Mouth to Neck Committee Angle，lit. drum up one's belly，four-sided footrim。The interior and exterior of the body and the footrim are glazed with Tung-ching glaze.，Symmetrically placed cross ears on both sides of the neck，Apricot-shaped projections on both anterior and posterior sides of the abdomen。Signed in blue and white regular script on the outside“大the Qing dynasty (1840-1861)年制”Six-character paragraph in two lines。　　Almond round vase is a traditional variety of China's ancient porcelain，Almost every dynasty since the Yongzheng period of the Qing Dynasty has been firing，An apricot-ring vase of the Xuantong period, with existing kiln-formed glazes、imitation of official glaze、Dongqing glaze and other varieties，all are well made，Reflecting the end of the Qing dynasty feudal ruler's extravagant life with porcelain。
描述_ZN: A gilt-painted Eastern blue-glazed floral pourer in the form of a rooster, Qianlong, Qing dynasty, 18.3 cm high, 2.3 cm in diameter.　　The floral watering is in the form of a rooster, with an upright head and a long tail hanging to the ground, carrying a crank-handled gallows vase on its back, the beak of the rooster as a stream, and the mouth of the vase as a watering hole. The entire body of the vase is glazed with eastern blue glaze, and the wings of the chicken are depicted in gold paint all over the body of the vase, and the banana leaves and chi dragons are depicted in gold paint on the body of the vase.　　The famous poet Li Bai of the Tang dynasty wrote in his "Dreaming of a trip to Tianwu": "I saw the sea sun on the half wall, and heard the heavenly rooster in the air". This flower waterer is a heirloom vessel from the Qing Dynasty court, with a small and delicate shape and meticulous gilding, reflecting the noble atmosphere of royal vessels. The vessel can be used for watering flowers, and can also be placed in the hall as a decoration vessel, combining practicality and ornamental qualities.
